FINAL BLOCK LAYOUT (net/kernels/kda_ut_solve.py::_block_specs — the only place block_shape/index_map/grid live): grid = (H, N // bn); in_specs = [BlockSpec((None, C, C), lambda h, j: (h, 0, 0)), BlockSpec((None, C, bn), lambda h, j: (h, 0, j))]; out_specs = BlockSpec((None, C, bn), lambda h, j: (h, 0, j)). Block shapes now carry one entry per array dimension (3 for both (H, C, C) and (H, C, N)) — the reported rank defect is fixed.

WHY THE HEAD AXIS IS SQUEEZED (None) AND NOT (1, C, C): Pallas drops Squeezed dims from the ref shape (_get_ref_block_shape), so the kernel body still receives exactly the (C, C) factor and the (C, bn) RHS slice that _solve_head was written for. With (1, C, C) the refs gain a leading size-1 axis and the body needs a reshape — a change to the math path, which the task forbade ('only block/index/grid'). Coverage is identical under either encoding (Blocked(1) with index h gives start 1*h = h). Confirmed on the host: the (1, C, C) + integer-indexed-subref variant does not even trace (a Ref indexed by an int yields a value, not a ref: 'Can only call load on a Ref: JitTracer').

WHY THE GRID COVERS ALL H (asserted mechanically, not by eye): grid dim 0 is H and the head dim is squeezed, so its index-map value h is the ELEMENT index — jax _get_start_index: Squeezed|Element -> start = index, Blocked -> start = block_size * index — i.e. grid program h owns head h and only h, for h in range(H): every head exactly once, no gap, no overlap, no program reaching outside range(H). Dim 1 (C) is taken whole (block == dim, index 0, so exactly one block). Dim 2 is tiled by bn with block index j in range(N // bn), and valid_config guarantees bn | N and bn a power of two, so the tiles partition the RHS exactly. test_pallas_block_specs_tile_every_array_dimension checks rank, tile-alignment and exact coverage for all three specs over every bn the sieve admits, plus a one-writer check on the output spec (no two programs write the same block, which would be a race, not just a coverage defect).

SECOND DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, beyond the architect's diagnosis — same family, also inside the allowed zone: the RHS index map used an ELEMENT offset j * bn where the framework requires a BLOCK index j (start = bn * index). The original pair (C, bn) + (h, 0, j*bn) would have started the RHS tiles at bn*j*bn — for bn=64, N=256 that is columns 0, 4096, 8192, 12288, i.e. out-of-bounds reads and tiles 1..3 never written (measured on the host: NaN in 2 of 4 output tiles). Fixed to j. Evidence: (a) the rule is identical in both jax 0.10.2 code paths — core.compute_start_indices_interpret and triton/lowering._get_start_index; (b) reproduced numerically on the host through interpret=True; (c) the skill's own template triton_matmul.py uses block indices (lambda i, j: (i, j)), the project's convention. Had only the rank been fixed and j*bn kept, the GB10 check would have failed again — with NaN/garbage instead of a clean block-shape error.
